notes: D-A1 RESOLUTION — ACCEPTED AS DIAGNOSIS, WITH THE EVIDENCE OBLIGATION IT CREATED LEFT OPEN. I accept the integration engineer's finding and withdraw D-A1 as a lens defect. The instrumentation is dispositive in a way my predecessor's pixel measurement could not be: all four profiles were instrumented and found bit-identical — one camera, matching FOVs, canopy approximately 690px everywhere — and the 300px frames exist only in strips captured at 01:20Z, before the D-10/D-13 autopilot fixes; replaying the same plans now yields full-size canopies. That is a coherent causal account (the pre-fix autopilot put the ship somewhere the post-fix autopilot does not, and the rig held screen anchors correctly the whole time), and it is confirmed by the mechanism my predecessor himself specified as the decisive probe: log the render camera per strip frame per profile. D-A1 is therefore reclassified critical-lens-defect -> stale-evidence. BUT acceptance of the diagnosis is not acceptance of the evidence: my predecessor's own escalation stands — 'until the LOW and HIGH families share one lens, every composition verdict in verification-report.json is unfounded' — and the fix to an unfounded verdict is a re-measurement, not a reclassification. The strips must be regenerated post-fix and EVERY composition verdict measured from them re-taken, specifically including the 31.8% spine reading that motivated ruling [e]'s 28-34% band. I sign the band because it is the honest expression of the shot's own intent at the shutter range, not because the 31.8% measurement survived; if the regenerated strips disagree with 28-34%, that is a contract question routed back to me, not an integrator judgement call.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE V6 ROUTED DEFECT: the same instrumentation bears on my draft-v6 STANDING condition (MEDIUM+reduced-motion reporting appliedFovDeg 75 where the other three tiers report 70). 'All four profiles bit-identical with matching FOVs' would discharge it, but the v6 defect was found by reading appliedFovDeg while D-A1 was found by measuring pixels, and I will not let one result close the other by implication. The condition stays STANDING until the post-fix four-variant state trace shows transit appliedFovDeg 70 on MEDIUM+reduced-motion explicitly.

AMENDMENT RECORD (v7), my lane: six rulings on the independent audit, all landed verbatim. [a] The audit was right that still-seam-of-light is not the seam — it was shot at range 955 with the station already resolved, so the three-distance thesis (dot -> line -> place) had no line. The new criterion makes the seam a LATCH-time capture with a falsifiable line test (7.5-8.2 degrees long, at most 2.4 degrees thick, no resolvable hull mass) plus a paired LOW frame, so the middle distance can never again be proved by a resolve frame. [b] The ST-0 still violated its own spec (camera at the Kestrel, no hearth in frame) and lost its subject to a large warm disc; the staging deltas re-tie the camera to the hearth (at most 25 units from the habitat-core handle, emissive in the bottom 20%) and the luminance claim is now a frame test — peak luminance is the frame maximum above the horizon band — rather than an unmeasurable 'above the brightest star'. Widening moon exclusion from 10 to 15 degrees of yaw is what buys that test its headroom. [c] galaxyInFrame:false was a name test that a purple nebula walked straight through; the replacement is perceptual and pixel-measured, and the berth ring — dock-offer geometry standing under a run whose whole claim is that no door is offered — is now suppressed under the docking predicate rather than merely un-centered. [d] and [f] convert two of my assertions into probes. [e] repairs my own prose in the direction the audit indicated. In three of the six the audit found my sentence wrong and my staging right; in [b] and [c] it found the frame wrong. Both verdicts are accepted.

WHAT THE [c] EDIT DID NOT LOSE, checked because a name-test removal can quietly take a real exclusion with it: v6's cut-line criterion ended 'no galaxy, planet or home fire in frame', and v7 replaces that whole clause with the perceptual term. The exclusion itself survives undamaged at two other sites — shots[11]/focalHierarchy/negativeSpaceIntent still reads 'no galaxy, no planet, no home fires in frame — both fires are explicitly behind the camera, which is K11's geometry made literal', and the GALAXY FIREWALL at evidence/acceptanceCriteria/9 still binds both transit HIGH stills. The capture criterion now tests dominance and the shot still tests absence; nothing was traded away.

DOC-DRIFT OBSERVATION, non-blocking, routed to the next cycle rather than patched here (patching it would be authorship): four sites still carry the mobile figure 'about 26% of frame width' — story/agencyWindows/6/mobileBehavior, variants/mobile/preservedFocalSubject, shots/11/framing/mobileSafeArea, shots/11/lens/mobileCropRisk. That 26% was derived as the 844x390 counterpart of the old desktop 31%. Ruling [e] replaced the desktop figure with a 28-34% band, and shots[11]'s occupancy intent now says only 'narrower at 844x390' with no number. Scaling the old pair's ratio onto the new band gives roughly 23.5-28.5%, so 26% falls inside it and no site is contradicted, no staging changes, and the mobile terms remain satisfiable as written. But 26% is now a number that has outlived its derivation — exactly the D-A7 failure class — and if the verifier is asked to measure mobile occupancy against a band it must be re-derived by me first.
